'''Benjamin John Eggleton''', {{post-nominals|country=AUS|FAA|FTSE|FOSA|FIEEE|FSPIE|FAIP|FRSN}}, (born 6 November 1970)<ref name="cv">{{cite web|title=Curriculum Vitae: Benjamin John Eggleton|url=http://api.profiles.sydney.edu.au/AcademicProfiles/profile/resource?urlid=benjamin.eggleton&type=cv|publisher=University of Sydney|access-date=11 January 2018}}</ref> is Professor in the [[University of Sydney School of Physics|School of Physics]] at the University of Sydney, where he leads a research group in [[integrated photonics]], [[nonlinear optics]] and smart sensors<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sydney.edu.au/news-opinion/news/2022/11/10/head-of-sydney-nano-appointed-pro-vice-chancellor--research-.html#:~:text=Professor%20Ben%20Eggleton%20has%20been,its%20translation%20into%20meaningful%20impact. |title=Head of Sydney Nano appointed Pro-Vice-Chancellor (Research) |last=Leatherdale |first=Verity |date=10 November 2022 |publisher=Sydney University |access-date=19 November 2022}}</ref> and serves as co-director of the NSW Smart Sensing Network (NSSN).<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.zdnet.com/article/nsw-government-launches-smart-sensing-network/|title=NSW government launches Smart Sensing Network|work=ZDNet|last=Bindi|first=Tas|date=2 February 2017|access-date=19 December 2017}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Eggleton obtained the bachelor's degree (with honours) in Science in 1992 and PhD degree in physics from the [[University of Sydney]] in 1996. In 1996, he joined [[Bell Labs|Bell Laboratories]], [[Lucent Technologies]] as a Postdoctoral Member of Staff in the Optical Physics Department under the supervision of [[Richart E. Slusher|Dr Richart E. Slusher]]. In 1998 he transferred to the Optical Fiber Research Department as a Member of Technical Staff and was promoted to Technical Manager of the Fiber Gratings Group in 2000. He was then promoted to Research Director within the Specialty Fiber Business Division of Bell Laboratories, where he was engaged in forward-looking research supporting Lucent Technologies business in optical fiber devices.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sydney.edu.au/science/people/benjamin.eggleton.php|title=Professor Benjamin Eggleton|website=sydney.edu.au|access-date=19 December 2017}}</ref>

Eggleton returned to the University of Sydney in 2003 as a full Professor and ARC [[Federation Fellowship]] in the School of Physics. He was founding Director of the [[Centre for Ultrahigh Bandwidth Devices for Optical Systems|ARC Centre of Excellence for Ultrahigh bandwidth Devices for Optical Systems (CUDOS)]] and served as Director from 2003 to 2017. 

In 2009 Eggleton established the Institute of Photonics and Optical Science (IPOS) at the [[University of Sydney]] and was the Director from 2009 to 2018. He was an [[ARC Laureate Fellow]] and an ARC [[Federation Fellowship]] twice.

In 2016 Eggleton and Gooding established the NSW Smart Sensing Network (NSSN) as the inaugural NSW Innovation Network. Eggleton currently serves as co-director of NSSN.

From 2018 to 2022, Eggleton was Director of the [[The University of Sydney Nano Institute|University of Sydney Nano Institute (Sydney Nano)]].

Since 2022 he has served as Pro-Vice-Chancellor (Research) at the University of Sydney.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sydney.edu.au/news-opinion/news/2022/11/10/head-of-sydney-nano-appointed-pro-vice-chancellor--research-.html|title=Head of Sydney Nano appointed Pro-Vice-Chancellor (Research) }}</ref> The Pro-Vice-Chancellor (Research) has executive responsibility for pivotal areas of the university's Research Portfolio relating to research policy, performance and conduct including clinical trials, research reporting and compliance. The role has responsibility for research integrity and ethics management.

==Research==
Eggleton's research links fundamental to applied science and spans physics and engineering. He has made pioneering contributions to nonlinear optics and all-optical signal processing with recent breakthrough achievements in the nonlinear optics of periodic media, [[Slow light|slow-light]] in [[photonic crystal]]s and ultrafast planar waveguide [[nonlinear optics]].<ref name=":0">{{cite news|url=http://sydney.edu.au/news/science/397.html?newsstoryid=8572|first=Katynna|last=Gill|title=Professor Ben Eggleton wins Walter Boas Medal|website=sydney.edu.au|date=3 February 2012|access-date=19 December 2017}}</ref> His research into new classes of nonlinear waveguides has created a new paradigm for [[Photonic integrated circuit|photonic chip]] based ultrafast optical signal processing and his group holds various world records.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://sydney.edu.au/nano/research/flagship-projects/nanoscale-photonic-circuits.shtml|title=Nanoscale Photonic Circuits|website=sydney.edu.au|access-date=19 December 2017}}</ref>

Eggleton's breakthroughs in the nonlinear optics of [[chalcogenide glass]]es have led to his demonstrations of new ultrafast optical devices for telecommunications applications, record low-threshold [[supercontinuum|supercontinuum generation]] sources and on-chip parametric sources. His group reported the first demonstration of on-chip stimulated [[Brillouin scattering|Brillouin]] scattering,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Pant|first1=Ravi|last2=Poulton|first2=Christopher G.|last3=Choi|first3=Duk-Yong|last4=Mcfarlane|first4=Hannah|last5=Hile|first5=Samuel|last6=Li|first6=Enbang|last7=Thevenaz|first7=Luc|last8=Luther-Davies|first8=Barry|last9=Madden|first9=Stephen J.|date=25 April 2011|title=On-chip stimulated Brillouin scattering|url=https://www.osapublishing.org/abstract.cfm?uri=oe-19-9-8285|journal=Optics Express|volume=19|issue=9|pages=8285–8290|doi=10.1364/OE.19.008285|pmid=21643078|bibcode=2011OExpr..19.8285P |issn=1094-4087|hdl=10453/117325|s2cid=6082816|hdl-access=free}}</ref> and holds the record for on-chip SBS gain. His fundamental breakthroughs include the first demonstrations of Bragg [[soliton]] and Gap soliton formation in periodic media and of slow-light-enhanced nonlinear optics in photonic crystals.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Eggleton|first=Benjamin J.|year=1996|title=Bragg Grating Solitons|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.76.1627|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=76|issue=10|pages=1627–1630|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.76.1627|pmid=10060477|bibcode=1996PhRvL..76.1627E |url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Eggleton|first1=Benjamin J.|last2=Sterke|first2=C. Martijn de|last3=Slusher|first3=R. E.|date=1 November 1997|title=Nonlinear pulse propagation in Bragg gratings|url=https://www.osapublishing.org/abstract.cfm?uri=josab-14-11-2980|journal=JOSA B|volume=14|issue=11|pages=2980–2993|doi=10.1364/JOSAB.14.002980|bibcode=1997JOSAB..14.2980E |issn=1520-8540|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.abc.net.au/science/articles/2011/08/02/3282881.htm|title=Ben Eggleton, optical physicist|date=2 August 2011|publisher=Australian Broadcasting Corporation|access-date=19 December 2017}}</ref>

==Publications==
Eggleton is the author and coauthor of more than 580 journal publications, including articles in ''[[Nature Photonics]]'', ''[[Nature Physics]]'', ''[[Nature Communications]]'', ''[[Physical Review Letters]]'', ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'' and ''[[Optica (journal)|Optica]]'' and over 300 invited presentations. His journal papers have been cited 29,000 times according to [[Web of Science]] with an h-number of 93 (129 in Google Scholar) and has filed over 45 patents.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com.au/citations?user=V2cnMDEAAAAJ&hl=en|title=Benjamin J. Eggleton – Google Scholar Citations|publisher=Google Scholar|access-date=7 February 2021}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
Eggleton is a Fellow of the [[The Optical Society|Optical Society of America (OSA)]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.osa.org/en-us/awards_and_grants/fellow_members/recent_fellows/2003_fellows/|title=2003 OSA Fellows|website=osa.org|access-date=19 December 2017}}</ref> [[IEEE Photonics Society|IEEE Photonics]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://theinstitute.ieee.org/technology-topics/consumer-electronics/introducing-the-class-of-2010648|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170819233950/http://theinstitute.ieee.org/technology-topics/consumer-electronics/introducing-the-class-of-2010648|url-status=dead|archive-date=19 August 2017|title=Introducing the Class of 2010 – IEEE – The Institute|website=[[IEEE]]|access-date=19 December 2017}}</ref> the [[Australian Academy of Technological Sciences and Engineering]] (ATSE),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sydney.edu.au/news/science/397.html?newsstoryid=4191|title=Prof Ben Eggleton elected Fellow of the Australian Academy of Technological Sciences and Engineering|website=sydney.edu.au|access-date=19 December 2017}}</ref> and the [[Australian Academy of Science]] (AAS).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.science.org.au/fellowship/fellows/professor-benjamin-john-eggleton|title=Professor Benjamin John Eggleton|publisher=Australian Academy of Science|access-date=19 December 2017}}</ref>

|url-status=dead }}</ref>
Eggleton was recipient of the 2017 University of Sydney Vice Chancellors Award for Outstanding Research.

Eggleton, together with a team of researchers from the [[University of Sydney]] and the [[Australian National University]], won the [[Australian Museum]]'s 2020 Defence Science and Technology [[Eureka Prizes|Eureka Prize]] for Outstanding Science in Safeguarding Australia.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=2020 Australian Museum Eureka Prize winners|url=http://australian.museum/get-involved/eureka-prizes/2020-eureka-prizes-winners/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201124093149/https://australian.museum/get-involved/eureka-prizes/2020-eureka-prizes-winners/ |archive-date=24 November 2020 |access-date=2020-12-09|website=The Australian Museum|language=en}}</ref> In 2022 Eggleton was recognized as Academic of the Year at the 2022 Defence Industry Awards.

Eggleton was President of the Australian Optical Society from 2008 to 2010. He was Editor-in-Chief for [[Optics Communications]] from 2007 to 2015 and was the Editor-in-Chief for [[APL Photonics]] from 2016-2025. Eggleton served on the Board of Governors for the [[IEEE Photonics Society]] from 2015 to 2017
